STANDARD  SAFETY  PRECAUTIONS 
 
 
Document No.  MMI-03 
October 2012 
By :  KK 
Rev.  01 
 
App,d :  MH 
 
 
1 SAFETY INSTRUCTIONS 
 
1.1 
 A refrigeration compressor package, when operating, contains refrigerant gas and 
lubricant at both high pressures and high temperatures.  Refrigerant gas is also 
present at low temperatures and pressures.  Depending upon the application, liquid 
refrigerant may also be present.  Package contents will also be at elevated 
pressures when the package is idle.  It is imperative, therefore, that the operators 
be properly trained and thoroughly familiar with the operation of the plant, the 
hazards involved, and the correct countermeasures in the event of plant failure. 
 
1.2 
Given the above, and that the twin screw compressor is also driven at high speed, 
irrespective of other site safety requirements, as a minimum bare skin, eye and 
hearing protection should be applied prior to performing any operator or 
maintenance activities. 
 
1.3 
Refrigerants generally are classified as hazardous according to NOHSC criteria.  
When dealing with refrigerants, safe storage, handling and disposal precautions 
must be exercised in accordance with the requirements of the applicable Statutory 
Authorities, the prevailing site safety rules & regulations and the MSDS (material 
safety data sheet) provided in section 1.02 of this manual for the package 
refrigerant. 
 
1.4 
Lubrication oils generally are classified as non-hazardous according to NOHSC 
criteria.  Again, when dealing with lubrication oils, safe storage, handling and 
disposal precautions must be exercised in accordance with the requirements of the 
applicable Statutory Authorities, the prevailing site safety rules & regulations and 
the MSDS (material safety data sheet) provided in section 1.02 of this manual for 
the package lubricant. 
 
1.5 
When the refrigeration compressor is drained for maintenance, consideration and 
caution need to be exercised as to the progressive release of refrigerant gas from 
the lubricant retained within the package. 
 
1.6 
To minimise the risk of personal injury, always drain the oil inventory (after 
depressurising) and perform a nitrogen purge before opening the system. 
 
1.7 
It is recommended that pipeline spades be fitted to positively isolate the idle 
compressor when performing maintenance. 
 
1.8 
It is recommended that appropriate tags be fitted to the respective controls or 
components when the package or parts thereof are isolated for service or 
maintenance procedures to prevent injury from accidental starting or pressurized 
fluid escape through open piping.
